old: The baseline uses continuous three-channel ADC1 acquisition and circular DMA. The sample-time setting is \texttt{ADC\_SAMPLETIME\_39CYCLES\_5}. The foreground reads the buffer without waiting in \texttt{analogRead()}, so acquisition continues during command handling and control updates. The control loop can use the latest available samples without pausing for a conversion.
new: The baseline uses continuous three-channel ADC1 acquisition and circular DMA with the sample-time setting \texttt{ADC\_SAMPLETIME\_39CYCLES\_5}. Samples are transferred to memory in the background, so the foreground can read the latest available values without waiting in \texttt{analogRead()} while handling commands and control updates.
reason: Combines repeated explanations of acquisition and the removal of conversion waits.

old:
Adding voltage feedback allowed the burst command to respond to the sensed voltage instead of relying on manual adjustment. The controller could therefore increase or reduce energy transfer when the voltage changed under load.

The first implementation waited for each ADC conversion before continuing the control update. Conversion waits, UART handling, and other foreground work shared the same execution path and could delay the next duty adjustment.
new: Voltage feedback allowed the burst command to increase or reduce energy transfer as the sensed voltage changed under load, replacing manual adjustment. The first implementation waited for each ADC conversion before updating the command. These conversion waits shared the foreground execution path with UART handling and other work, delaying opportunities to adjust duty.
reason: Connects the benefit of feedback to the blocking implementation and its practical timing limitation.
facts_preserved: UART and foreground work also affect timing

old:
Load removal leaves limited discharge through the connector, so further bursts can raise the bulk voltage. Average transfer was capped while minimum burst duration was retained to avoid truncating individual carrier cycles.

The no-load guard uses the primary-current indication at PA2 and the configured reference conditions to select a narrower band and lower high-duty cap. The defaults are \(V_{\mathrm{set}}=\SI{28}{\volt}\), \(V_{\mathrm{NLdrop}}=\SI{5}{\volt}\), and \(d_{\mathrm{NL}}=\SI{5}{\percent}\), giving approximately \SI{23}{\volt} to \SI{28}{\volt} at the secondary bulk. These defaults apply to the secondary bulk supply; the USB-C output has its own voltage setting.
new: After load removal, limited discharge through the connector allows continued bursts to raise the bulk voltage. The no-load guard uses the primary-current indication at PA2 and configured reference conditions to select a narrower voltage band and lower high-duty cap. Average transfer is thereby limited while the minimum burst duration is retained to avoid truncating individual carrier cycles. The defaults are \(V_{\mathrm{set}}=\SI{28}{\volt}\), \(V_{\mathrm{NLdrop}}=\SI{5}{\volt}\), and \(d_{\mathrm{NL}}=\SI{5}{\percent}\), giving approximately \SI{23}{\volt} to \SI{28}{\volt} at the secondary bulk. The USB-C output has its own voltage setting.
reason: Combines the cause of post-removal charging with the guard selection and burst constraint before giving the thresholds.
facts_preserved: PA2 and configured reference conditions select guard
All default values and bulk versus USB-C distinction retained

old: Each save appends a sequence-numbered, checksummed entry and verifies it by reading it back. Occupied entries are skipped after interrupted programming. Successive saves use different entries across the sector. The sector is erased when the journal wraps. An interruption during erase can still remove the saved configuration. Defaults then load with output OFF if no valid entry remains. Writes wait until output, startup, and autotuning are inactive so flash work does not interrupt live conversion.
new: Each save appends a sequence-numbered, checksummed entry and verifies it by reading it back. Occupied entries are skipped after interrupted programming, and successive saves use different entries across the sector. When the journal wraps, the sector is erased; an interruption during erase can remove the saved configuration. If no valid entry remains, defaults load with output OFF. Writes wait until output, startup, and autotuning are inactive so flash work does not interrupt live conversion.
reason: Groups interrupted-write recovery and erase behavior by the operation that causes each outcome, retaining the conditions on writes.
facts_preserved: Output, startup and autotuning write conditions

old:
Incomplete setup records and repeat measurements prevent a numerical
uncertainty budget at every point. The workbook values are shown at their original precision. Error bars are
omitted because the required uncertainty data are incomplete. Worst-case transients require repeated events and a defined
acceptance band, thermal equilibrium requires a temperature history, and
jitter requires measured timing. These limits apply throughout
Chapter~\ref{ch:results}.
new: Incomplete setup records and repeat measurements prevent a numerical uncertainty budget at every point. Workbook values are shown at their original precision, and error bars are omitted where the required uncertainty data are incomplete. Repeated events and a defined acceptance band are needed for worst-case transients; a temperature history is needed for thermal equilibrium, and measured timing is needed for jitter. These limits apply throughout Chapter~\ref{ch:results}.
